title: QuantScript
description: The Indicator Smithery: every indicator script viewed, edited and versioned, checked in a sandbox before it lands in the registry — and the forge that certifies them

capabilities.name: list
capabilities.description: Every indicator script of the Smithery (QuantScript/indicators/*.py) with the classes it holds, the registry keys they register, each key's certification (score, grade, certified — the worst track), the version history counts, and the archive of deleted scripts. Compact by default: hypotheses, defaults and per-track verdicts are left out — read a script or the QuantAlgo registry for those. Indicator scripts are private, discovered from the active library, and excluded from the installer.

refresh.description: Re-read the registry and re-probe Python instead of answering from the cache.

compact.description: Default true. false returns the full registry view of every class (hypothesis, defaults, parameter space, per-track verdicts) — large.

capabilities.name: read
capabilities.description: One script's source with its SHA-256 and latest recorded version. Opening records a baseline version on first sight and an 'external' version when the file changed outside QuantScript since the last one. contract.py (the contract every script obeys) can be read too, read-only.

file.description: The script's file name, e.g. extremes.py — no path.

capabilities.name: check
capabilities.description: Verify a candidate version of a script WITHOUT writing it: syntax (line and column), then a sandbox copy of the whole package imports the registry with the candidate in place and runs every registered class of the file through the contract — a signal() pass on a synthetic regime frame; depth 'full' adds the causality and scale-invariance validators. 'blocking' = must not be saved (syntax, import, cannot register); failed laws are reported. Roughly 1.3 s (quick) to 2 s (full).

file.description: The script's file name the candidate would replace (or a new <key>.py).

capabilities.name: save
capabilities.description: Write a script as a new version. The quick check runs first in the sandbox; a candidate that would not import or cannot register comes back with saved=false and its check attached, and nothing is written. Unchanged content returns unchanged=true. The versions history is append-only. A running QuantSystems engine loads the registry at start and needs a restart to see the change; QuantAlgo reloads by itself.

file.description: The script's file name, e.g. extremes.py, or indicators/__init__.py as __init__.py.

capabilities.name: versions
capabilities.description: A script's version history, newest first: version number, SHA-256, size, message, author (baseline | user | external | restore | template | delete | agent), whether it passed the sandbox check, and when. No content — use read_version for that.

capabilities.name: read_version
capabilities.description: One recorded version of a script with its full content — for a diff against the current file, or to bring back what a deleted script held.

capabilities.name: restore
capabilities.description: Write an earlier version back as a NEW version (checked like a save, never a rewind). Restoring the latest version of a deleted script recreates the file.

capabilities.name: create
capabilities.description: A new indicator script from the QuantScript template — a complete EMA-distance regime rule with hysteresis that passes every contract law — written as <key>.py and registering `key` through REGISTER / WARMUP (no edit of indicators/__init__.py). The key is checked against the registry in the sandbox first; a taken key is refused. Edit the hypothesis and the mechanism afterwards with save.

key.description: The registry key: a letter, then lowercase letters, digits and underscores (at most 40) — what a strategy passes to self.regime(key).

name.description: Display name (the class's `name`); defaults to the class name.

capabilities.name: delete
capabilities.description: Delete a script made in the suite (registration 'discovered', or one that registers nothing). Its last content is recorded as a final 'delete' version first, so the archive keeps it and restore can bring it back. The forge's explicit modules (imported by indicators/__init__.py), the registry file and the contract are refused.
